source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Locate any previous inspection records of the building, including any accessibility compliance checks or audits. Gathering this existing data will give you a baseline understanding of the structure and prior official findings.

3. List the date, time, and personnel involved in the current inspection.
Detailing this information ensures clarity and traceability of the inspection event.

4. Use a standardized checklist tailored to building accessibility.
This should cover all major accessibility topics, such as:

   a. Entrance accessibility: ramps, door width, automatic doors, etc.
   b. Pathway accessibility: clear path to all areas, tactile indicators at stairs, etc.
   c. Interior accessibility: door width, adequate turning space, accessible restrooms, etc.
   d. Stairways and ramps: handrails, proper slope, and landings.
   e. Elevators and lifts: adequate number, size, controls accessible, etc.
   f. Restrooms: accessible stalls, grab bars,
